chunks: 1686 - And he, peace be upon him, said:

“I found kindness to be true to its name, and nothing is better than kindness except its reward, and that is what is intended from it. Not everyone who loves to do kindness to people does it, and not everyone who desires it is able to do it, nor is everyone who is able to do it given permission concerning it. So when desire, ability, and permission come together, then happiness is complete for the seeker and the one to whom it is done.”

key_terms.الرَّغْبَةُ: the desire and willing inclination to perform good
key_terms.السَّعَادَةُ: felicity and true happiness resulting from fulfilled good
key_terms.الْإِذْنُ: permission or granted opportunity to act
key_terms.الْقُدْرَةُ: the ability or capacity to carry out the good deed
key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفَ: kindness, goodness, and recognized virtuous conduct toward others
key_terms.ثَوَابُهُ: its reward, especially the recompense granted by Allah

ai.seo_question: What does Imam عليه السلام teach about the conditions for doing good deeds and acts of kindness?
ai.summary: The Imam عليه السلام teaches that al-ma‘ruf, or kindness and good conduct, truly lives up to its name, and its greatest value lies in the divine reward attached to it. He explains that doing good depends on the convergence of inward desire, practical ability, and granted opportunity, and when these come together, both the doer and recipient partake in felicity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: “I found kindness to be true to its name, and nothing surpasses kindness except its reward, which is the ultimate purpose of it. Not everyone who desires to perform kindness towards others succeeds in doing so. Not everyone who seeks it is able to fulfill it, and not everyone who is capable of it is granted permission to act. When desire, ability, and permission come together, happiness is then complete for both the one seeking to give and the one receiving it."
